Quick notes after an initial look at the logs + dashboards (link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/latency?panel=mediapro-429-spike):
- There was a short-lived spike in request rate at 08:10 PT that exceeded the per-VM soft concurrency windows — autoscaler did not add capacity fast enough, resulting in a queue + 429 responses from the front proxy (rate-limiter kicking in)
- Concurrently we saw an increase in long-tail token generation times (~3x baseline) for the model variant they were pinned to — likely longer sequences from a marketing campaign
- Idle stream disconnects appear to be client-side timeouts in combination with upstream proxy keepalive settings at 30s. The runtime still had tokens being produced but the client closed the connection. This triggers retry storms from the client which amplifies the spike.

Proposed immediate mitigations (0–2 hours):
1) Temporarily increase the front-proxy soft concurrency threshold for MediaPro routes and bump their instance pool by +1 to absorb the burst.
2) Patch proxy keepalive to 60s for their route to reduce idle disconnects (config change).
3) Ask MediaPro to increase client-side timeout/backoff to 90s while we stabilize.

I can push a config change for (1) and (2) with a 15m window and monitor. Will add logs to JIRA INF-1629.

— Dev
